To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Tfcp2l is a transcriptional master regulator that coordinates cell type patterning in the mouse kidney, acting both in an autocrine manner in ICs and in a paracrine manner in PCs.
Tfcp2l is a critical regulator in the development of collecting ducts and the patterning of its epithelia.
Tfcp2l is required for the development of intercalated cells in the collecting duct.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the kidney and more precisely with the development of collecting duct cells.
the mechanisms that control cell fate and cell type diversity in the kidney.
the molecular and cellular basis of kidney disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Tfcp2l is a key transcription factor that is essential for the patterning of the collecting ducts.
Tfcp2l inactivation deletes IC cells, whereas Jag1 deletion results in the forfeiture or IC and PC identities.
Tfcp2l is a key transcription factor that controls the patterning of cells in the mouse collecting ducts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Tfcp2l is a critical regulator that controls IC-PC pattering.
Tfcp2l is a key regulator of IC and PC patterning.
Tfcp2l inactivation deletes IC, whereas Jag1 ablation results in forfeiture of discrete IC & PC identities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a transcription factor can act in a cell type specific manner to pattern cells in a salt and pepper epithelium.
the collecting duct is a unique nephron segment in that its epithelium is composed of at least two cell types: principal and intercalated cells.

the collecting duct epithelium is a unique nephron segment in the kidney, because it consists of two distinct cell types: principal and intercalated cells, which regulate salt and water homeostasis, and acid-base balance, respectively.
